editorial:
You probably upgrade your phone without thinking. This documentary follows that old device from your drawer to dumps in Ghana, showing workers burning wires and picking apart circuit boards. It feels personal because it starts with everyday tech and turns into a global story about hidden costs. The cinematography is clean, not flashy, and lets the images speak.

Standout elements include clear explanations, real human faces, and honest pros and cons. The pros are eye-opening facts, easy-to-follow science, and strong visuals. The cons are heavy scenes, a slower middle, and no simple fix. Watch it if you care about the environment or your tech habits. For the best picture, stream in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, the film returns to a UK family upgrading their gadgets, then cuts to a young worker in Ghana breaking apart a phone for tiny bits of metal. The twist is that much of what people call recycling is really dumping and burning in unsafe places. The ending leaves you with a direct challenge: buy less, repair more, and make sure your old electronics go to real recyclers instead of hidden dumps.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who wants to understand where old electronics really go.
